
### IPv6 packet format 

::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv6-packet-format.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Diagram of IPv6 header contents: (after lower layer header) byte '6', diffserv/ECN, flow label, payload length, next header, hop limit/TTL, source IPv6 address (128 bits), destination IPv6 address (128 bits), extension headers (variable), then next layer's stuff"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv6-packet-format.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="highlighting 'next header' field"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv6-packet-format.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="highlighting 'payload length' field"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv6-packet-format.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="highlighting 'hop limit/TTL' field"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv6-packet-format.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 fig-alt="highlighting 'diffserv/ECN' and 'flow label' fields"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv6-packet-format.figure-6.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=6 fig-alt="highlighting 128-bit source and destination address fields"}


:::

::: {.myoverbox .midlow .fragment fragment-index=2 .fade-in-then-out}

*  if "extension header" present, identifies first extension header type
   *  extension header idea similar to TCP "options" we saw earlier
*  otherwise, type of next layer header (TCP, UDP, etc.)

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=3 .fade-in-then-out}

*  payload = everything after fixed part of header
   *  includes extension headers AND next layer's data

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=4 .fade-in-then-out}

*  TTL = "time-to-live"
*  limits how many times packet is forwarded
*  used to prevent "routing loops"

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=5 .fade-in-then-out}

*  diffserv (differentiated services)/flow label
   *  optional hints for routers/switches about how important packet is
*  ECN = explicit congestion notification
   *  optional hints to support congestion control (later topic)

:::

### IPv4 packet format 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv4-packet-format.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Diagram of IPv4 header contents: (after lower layer header) byte '4', header length, diffserv/ECN, total length, identification, flags, fragment offset, hop limit/TTL, protocol, header checksum, source IPv4 address, destination IPv4 address, source IPv4 address (32 bits), destination IPv4 address (32 bits), options (variable)"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv4-packet-format.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="highlighting 'header length' and 'total length'"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv4-packet-format.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="highlighting 'identification', 'flags',  and 'fragment offset'"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv4-packet-format.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="highlighting 'protocol'"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv4-packet-format.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 fig-alt="highlighting 'hop limit/TTL'"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv4-packet-format.figure-6.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=6 fig-alt="highlighting 'header checksum'"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv4-packet-format.figure-7.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=7 fig-alt="highlighting source and destination address (each 32 bits)"}

![](/arp/texfig/ip-format-ipv4-packet-format.figure-8.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=8 fig-alt="highlighting 'diffserv/ECN'"}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=2 .fade-in-then-out}

*  data length = length of next layer's data only
*  header length includes variable 'options'

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=3 .fade-in-then-out}

*  these fields for "fragments" support
   *  packet sent in multiple pieces
*  also exists in IPv6, but IPv6 uses extension headers for it
*  we'll revisit fragments later

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=4 .fade-in-then-out}

*  identifier for which protocol: common: TCP, UDP, ICMP

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=5 .fade-in-then-out}

*  "time-to-live"/hop limit
*  same idea as IPv6

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=6 .fade-in-then-out}

*  checksum of header only
*  IPv6 got rid of IP-level checksums entirely
   *  probably because TCP, UDP, etc. do their own checksums anyways
   *  (and these checksums include IP source/destination addresses)

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=8 .fade-in-then-out}

*  same field format as IPv6

:::
